summary: Segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 as 802.1Q sub-interfaces over the shared eth1 link, with node1 (VyOS) routing between the two VLANs. node1: eth1 vif 10 = 10.10.10.254/24, vif 20 = 10.10.20.254/24 (committed and saved). node2: eth1.10 = 10.10.10.11/24 with a specific route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254. node3: eth1.20 = 10.10.20.12/24 with a specific route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.254 (specific routes chosen over a full default-route gateway so node2/node3 keep their existing internet egress via eth0). Verified bidirectional cross-VLAN ping with ttl=63 confirming a routed hop through node1, and that internet egress was undisturbed. Then performed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, then node2, then node3): captured baseline boot_id per node, triggered a background-scheduled native reboot on each, polled until the node's command execution returned, confirmed a new boot_id proving a genuine restart, and verified VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity fully recovered after each restart before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (VyOS), node2 (RHEL7), node3 (RHEL7) network state: all three share eth1 as an unconfigured second NIC alongside eth0 (the management/egress network)
Configured VyOS on node1: 802.1Q vif 10 (10.10.10.254/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.254/24) on eth1, committed and saved to config.boot
Configured node2: eth1.10 VLAN sub-interface (10.10.10.11/24) via ifcfg scripts, persistent 8021q module load via /etc/modules-load.d, and a specific static route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254
Configured node3: eth1.20 VLAN sub-interface (10.10.20.12/24) via ifcfg scripts, persistent 8021q module load, and a specific static route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.254

Corrected an initial mistake where GATEWAY= in the ifcfg-eth1.10/20 files created a competing zero-metric default route that would have hijacked node2/node3's internet-bound traffic away from eth0; replaced with route-eth1.NN files scoping only the peer VLAN subnet
Verified cross-VLAN ping (ttl=63, confirming the packet was routed through node1) in both directions, and confirmed internet egress via eth0's default route was undisturbed on both node2 and node3
Captured baseline kernel boot_id on all three nodes before any restart

Restarted node1: background-scheduled `reboot`, polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirmed new boot_id, verified VLAN interfaces and firewall/forwarding config persisted via config.boot, and re-verified cross-VLAN ping from node2 and node3 recovered
Restarted node2: background-scheduled `sudo reboot`, polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1.10 address/route persisted and cross-VLAN ping to node3 recovered

Restarted node3: background-scheduled `sudo reboot`, polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1.20 address/route persisted and cross-VLAN ping to node2 recovered from both sides
